items.title: Jane Ira Bloom interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 3, 1998
items.q: I remember talking with Billy Taylor about this in that interview

ctx.x: In New York is there any kind of racial scene connected with jazz that is uncomfortable or is there any issues about race these days in the music that you’ve been able to see?

Well if you were to look, as time has gone on, whether the music community has been polarized into black and white, I’ve felt that a lot, when it did exist, and when I saw it, it seemed like it was the musicians who are not in control of it, it felt like the music business community, the promoters, the club owners, were having more input into this, and the critics as well too I think, than I think the musicians. And that was a scary moment, a scary perception. That choices were being made about who musicians…
That there was control being exerted from—
